title: Splitting of an injection measured on a free presentation of the cokernel
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, $u:N\to M$ an injective homomorphism of $R$-modules, $Q=M/u(N)$ with projection $p:M\to Q$, and $F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\pi}Q\to0$ an exact sequence of $R$-modules with $F_0$ free. Let $\alpha:F_0\to M$ be an $R$-linear map with $p\circ\alpha=\pi$, and let $\beta:F_1\to N$ be the unique $R$-linear map with $u\circ\beta=\alpha\circ d_1$ (it exists since $p\circ\alpha\circ d_1=\pi\circ d_1=0$, so $\alpha\circ d_1$ takes values in $u(N)$, and it is unique since $u$ is injective). Then $u$ has an $R$-linear left inverse $v:M\to N$ ($v\circ u=\mathrm{id}_N$) if and only if there is an $R$-linear map $\gamma:F_0\to N$ with $\beta=\gamma\circ d_1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 02HO (lemma-split-injection-after-completion, lines 18148-18165): 'The extension above is split if and only if there exists a map gamma : F_0 -> N such that beta = gamma o d_1', stated there without proof
